newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Oct 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Oct 3.

text.p: WellPoint Health Networks Inc is on the verge of closing talks to buy most or all of John Hancock Life Insurance Co 's health-insurance operations, the Wall Street Journal reported Thursday.
* Talks broke down between auto workers and the Canadian unit of General Motors Corp as thousands of employees went on strike hours before the deadline set by their union.
* U.S. state regulators are wondering why some mutual funds that are shunning new investors keep imposing levy charges to pay for advertizing, marketing and distribution costs.
* Toys R Us Inc said it agreed to buy Baby Superstore Inc in a stock swap worth $410 million.
* Service Corp International said it will make an exchange offer to Loewen Group Inc shareholders and raise its bid to $45 a share in stock from $43.
* The Dow Jones industrial average rose 29.07 to 5,933.977, while the Standard & Poor's 500-stock index climbed 4.93 to 694.01, both of them setting records.
* Heating-oil futures prices rose to their highest levels since the Persian Gulf War after reports showed stock drawdowns.
* The Bank of Canada cut its bank rate a quarter percentage point.
* Charles Swab will steer business to fee-based financial advisers through employee referrals and an ad campaign.
* Viacom Inc is fighting back pressure from some big shareholders to spin off Blockbuster Entertainment.
* Bristol-Myers Squibb Co's Pravachol might benefit from recent scientific studies that found the drug could help maintain blood flow to the heart.
* Revlon Inc will merge its discount fragrance stores with Cosmetic Center Inc COSCA.O.
* Broderbund Software Inc named Joe Durrett as chief executive officer.
* Morgan Stanley Group Inc's profit increased 4.8 percent to $219 million in the latest quarter and its president, John Mack, assumed the new post of chief executive officer.
